## Individual heterogeneity within population stability

```{r}
#| label: tbl-agent-level
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Agent-level temporal dynamics demonstrating individual heterogeneity within population stability"
agent_vars <- c(
  "pss10" = "PSS-10 per agent-step",
  "resilience" = "Resilience level",
  "affect" = "Emotional state",
  "resources" = "Psychological resources",
  "current_stress" = "Stress intensity",
  "stress_controllability" = "Controllability perception",
  "stress_overload" = "Overload perception",
  "consecutive_hindrances" = "Hindrance streak length"
)
agent_sd <- sapply(names(agent_vars), function(col) sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", mean(a[[col]]), sd(a[[col]])))
agent_interp_vals <- sapply(names(agent_vars), agent_interp)
tbl2 <- data.frame(
  Variable = unname(agent_vars),
  `Mean ± SD` = agent_sd,
  Interpretation = agent_interp_vals,
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(tbl2, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
```

@tbl-agent-level reveals substantial dynamic variability within the
stable population framework. The contrast between population-level
stability (CVs from `r pop_cv("avg_resources")` to `r pop_cv("avg_affect")`) and
individual-level heterogeneity (CVs from `r agent_cv("pss10")` to
`r agent_cv("affect")`) exemplifies the dual nature of the modeled system.
Individual agents experience significant fluctuations in stress
(`r agent("current_stress")`, CV `r agent_cv("current_stress")`), resilience
(`r agent("resilience")`, CV `r agent_cv("resilience")`), and affect
(`r agent("affect")`). Its large CV reflects a mean near zero on the $[-1, 1]$ scale. The SD of `r sprintf("%.3f", sd(a$affect))` indicates moderate dispersion, but dividing by a near-zero mean inflates the ratio, making CV uninformative for this variable. These variations are constrained by social
interactions that maintain population equilibrium. Agents perceive their
stressors as largely controllable (`r agent("stress_controllability")`) and
rarely overwhelming (`r agent("stress_overload")`), capturing the
cognitive appraisal diversity that drives individual adaptation
strategies. Hindrance streaks remain bounded
(`r agent("consecutive_hindrances")`, maximum
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(a$consecutive_hindrances))`), demonstrating the
system's capacity to prevent pathological cascades through network
support. Individual diversities are harmonized through social dynamics
to achieve collective stability: social network dynamics transform
individual variability into population-level equilibrium.
